Chi-square (or Fisher's exact) tests

Source: R/tests.R
cr_chisq.Rd

An overall test of association between an outcome and a grouping variable, with Cramer's V. For a binary outcome, pairs adds 2 x 2 comparisons between groups with the proportions, a correction across pairs, and Cohen's h.

Usage

cr_chisq(
  data,
  dv,
  group,
  pairs = NULL,
  ref = NULL,
  by = NULL,
  exact = "auto",
  success = NULL,
  adjust = "holm",
  dv_adjust = "none",
  conf_level = 0.95,
  labels = NULL,
  level_labels = NULL,
  dv_labels = NULL,
  clean_labels = TRUE
)

Arguments

data

A data frame.

dv

One or more outcome columns.

group

Grouping (condition) column.

pairs

NULL (overall test only), "all", "ref", or specific pairs.

ref

Reference level when pairs = "ref" (default: first level).

by

Optional column: run every comparison within each subgroup.

exact

"auto" (Fisher's exact test when any expected count is below 5), TRUE, or FALSE.

success

For pairwise comparisons, the outcome value counted as a success (default: the last level, TRUE, or 1).

adjust

Correction across the pairs of each outcome (any stats::p.adjust() method). When on, CIs (mean difference and d) are Bonferroni-adjusted to match, e.g. 98.3% CIs for 3 pairs, so a CI that excludes zero agrees with the corrected p. adjust = "none" gives ordinary 95% CIs.

dv_adjust

Correction across outcomes for each pair. CIs widen to match (Bonferroni across pairs x outcomes).

conf_level

Confidence level.

labels, level_labels, dv_labels, clean_labels

Display labels, as in clean_regress().

Value

A cr_tests object.
